articles.title: Los Cavaliers estarán en el Martín Carpena
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Cleveland, que hará una concentración en 'The Embassy', en Fuengirola, harán una exhibición abierta al público el 4 de octubre
articles.summary: El equipo de Cleveland, que hará una concentración en 'The Embassy', en Fuengirola, harán una exhibición abierta al público el 4 de octubre
articles.body: Tras varios días de entrenamiento y preparación en 'The Embassy', en Fuengirola (Málaga), los Cleveland Cavaliers disputarán un scrimmage abierto al público el domingo 4 de octubre, a las 12.00 horas, en el Palacio de Deportes José María Martín Carpena. El encuentro dará la bienvenida a jóvenes jugadores de clubes y academias locales, y ofrecerá a la comunidad del baloncesto malagueño la oportunidad de vivir la NBA de cerca, al tiempo que refuerza el vínculo de los Cavaliers con la ciudad y la región. El scrimmage se organiza en colaboración con The Embassy, el Ayuntamiento de Málaga, la Diputación de Málaga y la delegación malagueña de la Federación Andaluza de Baloncesto (FAB). Las entidades participantes distribuirán 10.000 entradas entre jóvenes de clubes y academias locales para este evento. Antes del scrimmage, los Cavaliers abrirán su Training Camp 2026, presentado por Cleveland Clinic, en The Embassy, en Andalucía, donde el equipo entrenará del 30 de septiembre al 3 de octubre. El campus marcará la primera vez que un equipo de la NBA celebra su training camp en España. Situado en Fuengirola, en la Costa del Sol, The Embassy es un centro de alto rendimiento de baloncesto concebido para este fin y diseñado por José Calderón, exjugador de la Selección Española y actual assistant general manager de los Cavaliers, junto a Berni Rodríguez, también exjugador de la Selección Española. El centro cuenta con aproximadamente 1.500 metros cuadrados de infraestructura profesional de baloncesto, incluidas dos pistas con estándar FIBA/NBA, un gimnasio de alto rendimiento, zonas de rehabilitación y fisioterapia, recursos de recuperación y tecnología audiovisual para el scouting y la preparación táctica. The Embassy ha sido también la sede de entrenamiento de The Sanctuary, el retiro anual de rendimiento en pretemporada organizado por PLYRS UNTD, la marca comercial de la National Basketball Players Association (NBPA). The Sanctuary regresó a Andalucía por quinto año consecutivo en julio y, a lo largo de ese periodo, ha reunido a más de 200 jugadores de la NBA en The Embassy para entrenamientos, sesiones de trabajo y partidos cinco contra cinco. Málaga y Andalucía ofrecen el escenario idóneo para el training camp de los Cavaliers: clima mediterráneo, un entorno deportivo y de bienestar de primer nivel, y la privacidad que necesita un equipo de la NBA para comenzar la temporada 2026-27. Ese entorno permitirá a los Cavaliers centrarse en el entrenamiento, construir la química del equipo y afianzar la camaradería antes de la campaña.

articles.title: LeBron James Wants to Give 'Blueprint' to Joel Embiid, Help Complete 'The Process' with 76ers
articles.summary: Thirteen years after the Philadelphia 76ers entered their "Trust the Process" era, LeBron James is focused on helping the franchise fulfill their ultimate goal by winning an NBA championship.
articles.body:
Thirteen years after the Philadelphia 76ers entered their "Trust the Process" era, LeBron James is focused on helping the franchise fulfill their ultimate goal by winning an NBA championship.

On the latest Mind the Game episode released Friday (starts at 15:45 mark), James explained he wants to give the "blueprint" of what it takes to win at the highest level to Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey in order to help the Sixers complete "the process" this season.

10 NBA Players With the Most to Lose at Training Camp 😓

Later in the episode (starts at 20:45 mark), James said Embiid's presence and a desire to help him win influenced his decision to sign with Philadelphia:

"He's done everything in our league. And the only thing he has not done — that's win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one. He's been the MVP of our league, has a gold medal, All-Stars, signature shoes, bunch of money, beautiful family. He has everything. He has the city on his back. It's been the process, you know, for what 10 years, 12 years or however long he's been there. articles.title: Yankuba Sima, opción seria para regresar al Unicaja
articles.standfirst: Las lesiones hacen que el conjunto malagueño se mueva en busca de un pívot
articles.summary: Las lesiones hacen que el conjunto malagueño se mueva en busca de un pívot
articles.body: El Unicaja arrancará este domingo (19:00 horas) su andadura en la Liga Endesa ante el Real Madrid en el Movistar Arena. Lo hará con tres bajas respecto al dibujo inicial de la plantilla: Nzosa, Kalinoski y Tyson Pérez. La lesión del hispano-dominicano, que apunta al quirófano, deja especialmente tocado el juego interior y obliga al club a mirar al mercado. Así lo confirmó Txus Vidorreta esta semana. Uno de los nombres que se estudia seriamente es el de Yankuba Sima. El pívot gerundense está negociando su salida del Valencia Basket, donde ha perdido protagonismo. Este jueves, de hecho, quedó fuera de la convocatoria de Xavi Albert para el debut en Euroliga ante el Besiktas, mientras sí entró el cubano Jasiel Rivero, con contrato temporal. Sima llegó el pasado verano a Valencia después de que el club pagase 500.000 euros al Unicaja por su fichaje. Su protagonismo ha sido escaso durante la temporada y su salida puede abrirle ahora la puerta de regreso a Málaga. El Unicaja no contemplaba esta posibilidad durante el verano, pero el escenario ha cambiado con las lesiones. Según avanzó SER Málaga y ha podido confirmar este medio, Sima es una opción que se está manejando en Los Guindos. Además de reforzar el juego interior, cuenta con la condición de cupo, un factor especialmente importante para la BCL tras las bajas de Tyson Pérez y Nzosa. Otro nombre que aparece en el radar es Killian Tillie. Vidorreta conoce al ala-pívot y valora su calidad, pero su situación física condicionó cualquier movimiento en verano. El francés pasó por quirófano por una lesión de rodilla y el Unicaja sigue de cerca su evolución. Si recupera plenamente la salud, podría volver a ser una alternativa.

articles.title: Vidorreta: "No podemos repetir ante el Real Madrid los errores del partido de pretemporada"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Unicaja valora positivamente el estado de ánimo de la plantilla antes del estreno del curso en la Liga Endesa
articles.summary: El entrenador del Unicaja valora positivamente el estado de ánimo de la plantilla antes del estreno del curso en la Liga Endesa
articles.body: El entrenador del Unicaja, Txus Vidorreta, ha analizado este viernes en rueda de prensa el estado del equipo antes del estreno en la Liga Endesa ante el Real Madrid el domingo a las 19:00 horas. El técnico se muestra confiado en que el equipo ofrezca una imagen diferente a la del enfrentamiento de pretemporada ante los blancos, que terminó con un contundente 74-113 en el XV Torneo Costa del Sol. Vidorreta ha comenzado valorando el estado de ánimo de la plantilla. “Es bueno. Estamos con mucha ilusión, con muchas ganas de empezar a competir, que para eso llevamos trabajando un mes y unos días en la estructura de la plantilla con muchas novedades. Vamos con mucha ilusión, con muchas ganas de competir bien, no solo en este partido, sino en todos, y de seguir en la línea que estamos marcando durante una gran parte de la pretemporada, de ser un equipo sólido, reconocible y con muchas ganas de empezar”. Sobre el Real Madrid, rival al que ya se midieron durante la pretemporada, el entrenador del Unicaja tiene claro qué debe cambiar respecto a aquel encuentro. “Sabemos perfectamente los aspectos en los que tenemos que mejorar, cuáles son las virtudes del Real Madrid y dónde cometimos errores que no debemos repetir. Esa es una información muy valiosa de cara a la preparación de un partido como el del domingo, primero por haber tenido la capacidad para analizar dónde estuvieron nuestros grandes problemas; segundo, la capacidad para reaccionar tanto contra el UCAM Murcia como contra el Monbus Obradoiro, no solo por ganar, sino porque volvimos a competir en la línea de lo que lo habíamos hecho contra La Laguna Tenerife; y en tercer lugar, porque es una motivación para los jugadores cuando, después de una derrota tan clara, tienen enseguida la oportunidad de demostrar que somos mucho mejores de lo que demostramos en el Torneo Costa del Sol”. Vidorreta también fue cuestionado sobre si el Unicaja está en disposición de competir de tú a tú con los equipos de nivel Euroliga. El técnico mantiene los pies en el suelo y pone como referencia la pasada temporada. “No sé si estamos más cerca, quiero pensar que sí. Tampoco parecía que el año pasado La Laguna Tenerife estaba en disposición de meterse en semifinales y nos metimos. Y el Asisa Joventut, que es otro equipo veterano y que juega un baloncesto ordenado para ganar, pues también se metió en semifinales y ahora acaba de ganar la Supercopa. Creo que como mi Unicaja va a ser un equipo que va a jugar bien, va a jugar para ganar y lo hará ordenado, vamos a tratar de trabajar todo el año para estar entre los ocho primeros, y si lo estás, pues ya estás cerca de los transatlánticos”.

articles.title: Moussa Kamissoko Commits to Syracuse MCBB, Program's 2nd 5-Star Prospect in Last Decade
articles.summary: The Syracuse University men's basketball program has landed one of its most significant recruits in years, securing a commitment from forward Moussa Kamissoko on Friday.
articles.body:
The Syracuse University men's basketball program has landed one of its most significant recruits in years, securing a commitment from forward Moussa Kamissoko on Friday.

According to ESPN's Jeff Borzello , Kamissoko informed ESPN's Paul Biancardi on Friday of his intention to play his college basketball for the Orange.

Kamissoko is rated as a 5-star prospect by 247Sports , as well as the No. 14 overall player in the class of 2027.

Coach K's Son-in-Law, Former Assistant Dies at 47

Per Borzello, Kamissoko is new Syracuse head coach Gerry McNamara's first 5-star recruit, and he is only the second 5-star player to commit to Syracuse over the past decade.

Syracuse was once considered to be among the premier college basketball programs in the country, winning the national championship in 2003 and reaching the Final Four on six occasions from 1975 to 2016.

However, the Orange have not reached the NCAA tournament since 2021, which was legendary head coach Jim Boeheim's third-to-last season at the helm.

Adrian Autry took over following Boeheim's retirement in 2023, and only managed a record of 49-48 over three seasons before getting fired.

The Orange went just 15-17 last season on the heels of a 14-19 mark in 2024-25, which was the program's worst record since the 1968-69 campaign.

In an effort to turn things around, Syracuse hired McNamara, who was a key figure as a guard on the Orange's 2003 national title game.

McNamara spent the past two seasons as the head coach at Siena, and he led the Saints to the NCAA tournament last season.

It is clear that McNamara is already making a massive impact on the program by bringing in a talent the caliber of Kamissoko.

A 6'7", 180-pound wing from Geneva, Ohio, Kamissoko drew interest from many of the top programs in college basketball.

Per 247Sports , Kamissoko had scholarship offers from Kentucky, UConn, Alabama, Illinois, Louisville, Baylor, Florida State and Virginia, among many others.

If Kamissoko is a sign of things to come for Syracuse under McNamara, then it may not be long before the Orange are once again a big-time factor in March Madness.

articles.title: NBA Exec Says Luka Doncic Can Reach 'Full Potential' with Lakers After LeBron James' Exit for 76ers
articles.summary: Being a 27-year-old with six top-eight MVP finishes on your resume wouldn't seem to leave a lot of room for growth, but at least one NBA executive believes Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić is poised to have the best season of his career.
articles.body:
Being a 27-year-old with six top-eight MVP finishes on your resume wouldn't seem to leave a lot of room for growth, but at least one NBA executive believes Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić is poised to have the best season of his career.

Per ESPN's Ben Golliver , the executive explained Dončić will reach his "full potential" now that James is no longer with the Lakers and expectations for the club have increased after their offseason additions.

"With LeBron [James] gone, the weight and expectations of the [Los Angeles] Lakers will push Luka to reach his full potential," the exec said. "He will take the MVP trophy home to Slovenia next summer."

10 NBA Players With the Most to Lose at Training Camp 😓

1 Trade To Fix a Contender's Biggest Flaw 🏀

Dončić is coming off a season in which he led the NBA in scoring average (33.5 points per game) and ranked third in assists (8.3). The Lakers won 53 games, their most in a season since 2010-11, and he finished fourth in MVP voting.

The argument for a fully-unlocked Dončić primarily stems from Walker Kessler's presence. Dončić reportedly made it known to Los Angeles' front office that Kessler was someone he wanted to play alongside.

Los Angeles paid a steep price to get Kessler in a sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz in which it gave up unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and first-round pick swaps in 2028 and 2030. Kessler also signed a four-year, $130 million contract with the Lakers.

The best season of Dončić's career thus far came in 2023-24 when the Dallas Mavericks gave him two rim-running centers by drafting Dereck Lively II and trading for Daniel Gafford midway through the year.

Kessler can fill that role for the Lakers and give them a defensive stopper in the paint that has been missing since Anthony Davis was traded.

There's no doubt Dončić is going to put up huge numbers because he has done that every year of his career, but his chemistry with new additions like Kessler and Quentin Grimes will determine if he hits the ceiling this executive expects from him.

articles.title: Aunque no sea una efeméride redonda, si el mejor mate in-game de siempre cumple años hay que recordarlo
articles.summary: Este 25 de septiembre se cumplen 26 años del mejor mate de todos los tiempos, el que hizo Vince Carter en los Juegos de Sidney saltando por encima de los 2,17 metros del pívot francés Frederic Weis. Una jugada que forma parte de la historia del baloncesto.
articles.body: Este 25 de septiembre se cumplen 26 años del mejor mate de todos los tiempos, el que hizo Vince Carter en los Juegos de Sidney saltando por encima de los 2,17 metros del pívot francés Frederic Weis. Una jugada que forma parte de la historia del baloncesto. El prodigioso salto de Carter, por entonces en los Raptors, le sorprendió incluso a él mismo. "Todo el mundo vio el mate, sin embargo, en ese momento, yo ni siquiera sabía qué había saltado sobre alguien", dijo el protagonista años después. Por entonces tenía 23 años y nadie habría pensado que iba a convertirse en el jugador más longevo en la historia de la NBA llegando hasta las 22 temporadas en activo. Carter recuerda así su acción más celebre: "Robé el balón, di dos pasos y salté, pero pensé que había saltado desde demasiado lejos, que iba a ser cazado y que iba a ser objeto de alguna campaña de burla. Por eso me excité tanto al conseguirlo, porque pensaba que no iba a machacar porque había saltado muy lejos". Aquello marcó un antes y un después en la capacidad humana para retar a la gravedad. Ya lo habían marcado mates firmados por Jordan, Wilkins o Erving, pero lo que hizo Carter, en pleno partido, la elevó a otra dimensión.

articles.title: Kyrie Irving Gives Injury Update, Latest on Mavericks Star's Status for 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: Dallas Mavericks star Kyrie Irving provided a new update regarding his knee injury as he prepares for the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks star Kyrie Irving provided a new update regarding his knee injury as he prepares for the 2026-27 season.

"No restrictions," Irving told reporters Friday. "Obviously there'll be some conversations with the medical staff about back-to-backs and the quality of where I am. Just being honest, day to day, and just having that fluid communication."

"Everyone's going to give me the support that I need," he added. "From a mental standpoint, coming back from a traumatic injury is not the easiest thing to overcome. But no excuses, I think I was built for this at a very young age."

Irving missed the entire 2025-26 season while recovering from a torn ACL that he suffered in March 2025.

The 34-year-old has been ramping up for his return by playing in summer pickup contests, per ESPN's Tim MacMahon .

Irving has continued to showcase his offensive prowess during the sessions, receiving praise from Brooklyn Nets forward Michael Porter Jr. after they participated in the same game.

"I was hooping with Kyrie yesterday, and this is off of his ACL," Porter said Aug. 24 on his Curious Mike podcast (h/t SI.com's Sameer Kumar ). "That dude was so cold, bro. I couldn't believe how he was moving out there. He was getting to the lane; there's all [seven] footers in there, and he was somehow [finishing] with the left. Bro, it was nutty. It was crazy."

Irving last played for the Mavericks during the 2024-25 season, averaging 24.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.3 steals per game while compiling 47.3/40.1/91.6 shooting splits.

He earned his ninth career All-Star nod for his efforts.

While Dallas is coming off a 26-56 finish last season, the team is looking to climb further up the Western Conference standings led by Irving and reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg.

The Mavericks will open their 2026-27 campaign against the Houston Rockets on Oct. 21.

articles.title: D'Angelo Russell Waived by Grizzlies, Top Landing Spots for PG in NBA Free Agency
articles.summary: D'Angelo Russell's time with the Memphis Grizzlies has come to an end before it ever really began.
articles.body:
D'Angelo Russell's time with the Memphis Grizzlies has come to an end before it ever really began.

Russell will become a free agent after being waived by the Grizzlies going into the start of training camp next week. ESPN's Shams Charania first reported the move.

Ranking the NBA's Best Young Cores Right Now 🔢

Assuming Russell wants to land with a team that has aspirations of being a playoff contender, potential destinations like the Miami Heat, Charlotte Hornets and Denver Nuggets have a need for depth in their backcourt.

The Heat are the most obvious potential destination for Russell. Their current point guard depth chart features Davion Mitchell, Dru Smith, Ryan Conwell and Tre Donaldson.

Mitchell is the only true point guard from that group, though Giannis Antetokounmpo figures to get plenty of run as the primary ballhandler for head coach Erik Spoelstra.

Given the injury issues Antetokounmpo had last season, the Heat may not want to put a lot on his plate too early in the season. Russell could slot in as the backup for Mitchell in Miami.

Charlotte recently added to its point guard rotation by acquiring Dennis Schröder from the Cleveland Cavaliers, so someone like Russell may not slot in with its current roster if the organization is confident in Coby White staying healthy.

White is penciled in as the Hornets' starting point guard, but he missed 32 games last season due to calf and groin injuries. Russell could provide depth at least through training camp as the coaching staff sees what the new-look roster after trading LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges looks like.

Last but not least, the Nuggets can use as much as depth at a low cost as they can get right now. Ownership was roundly criticized for seemingly prioritizing money over on-court success after sending Peyton Watson to the Cavs in a sign-and-trade deal last month.

Denver's starting five remains strong, particularly with Nikola Jokić, Jamal Murray and Aaron Gordon as the top three. Gordon's health and a potential bounce-back year from Christian Braun are crucial to how high the ceiling will be for the Nuggets.

Beyond that group, though, the Nuggets' depth falls off in a hurry. Tyus Jones, DeMar DeRozan and Marvin Bagley III will be counted on to play significant roles.

Denver's backup to Murray is a huge question mark right now. Jones, who at one point was regarded as the best backup point guard in the NBA, averaged 3.0 points and 2.4 assists per game in 48 appearances last season.

Russell is not that far removed from being an effective starter. He averaged 18.0 points on 41.5 percent three-point shooting and 6.3 assists per game in 76 appearances for the Los Angeles Lakers in 2023-24.

Things have fallen off for Russell in recent years, but the right situation could help him get back to being a starting-caliber player for a team that needs depth with the start of the regular season rapidly approaching on Oct. 20.

articles.title: D'Angelo Russell reportedly waived by Grizzlies 2 months after trade from Wizards
articles.summary: Russell's next team will be his fourth in the past two seasons.
articles.body:
D'Angelo Russell's time with the Memphis Grizzlies is over before he could even play a game.

According to ESPN's Shams Charania , Russell is being waived by the Grizzlies as the team needed flexibility with its roster. The 30-year-old guard was dealt to Memphis by the Washington Wizards in July as part of a trade involving six teams and 11 players .

The move has been coming as Yahoo Sports' Kelly Iko reported in July that the two sides were working together to help Russell find a new home. His next team will be his sixth since entering the NBA in 2015-16 with the Los Angeles Lakers — one of two teams, along with the Brooklyn Nets , where he's had two stints.

Russell played 26 games with the Mavericks last season, averaging a little over 19 minutes per night and 10.2 points, 4 assists and 2.3 rebounds.

After being dealt to the Wizards at the trade deadline, he did not play again during the 2025-26 season as the sides discussed a potential buyout. That never happened and Russell exercised his $6 million player option for this season before the summer trade.

articles.title: LeBron James Says 76ers Need to Put Egos Aside to Win NBA Title, 'Shouldn't Be No Misunderstanding'
articles.summary: LeBron James detailed the approach that he believes the Philadelphia 76ers need to take in order to win a championship during the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
LeBron James detailed the approach that he believes the Philadelphia 76ers need to take in order to win a championship during the 2026-27 season.

"One, it needs to be, 'What is our mission? What is our day-to-day mission? Are we bringing our personal egos to the table for the collective group, or are we bringing our egos to the table for the collective individual?' Because obviously we've all gotten to this point of our career for a reason, we're all who we are for a reason," James said Thursday on his Mind the Game podcast (39:30 mark). "But if we're coming together for one common goal, now if things happen and transpire we can look each other in the eye and say, 'This is how we said we was gonna go about it.' That's accountability."

"If what I've been hearing from the guys, that we're here to have championship habits and this is what we're part of, then there shouldn't be no misunderstanding," he added.

The 76ers enter next season with high expectations after adding James and Jaylen Brown to a starting lineup that already features Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

It'll be intriguing to see how all five players fit together, as Maxey averaged a team-high 28.3 points per game in Philadelphia last season. Brown also led the Boston Celtics with his scoring average of 28.7 points per game during his 2025-26 campaign.

Although Embiid was limited to just 38 games last year, he's averaged 27.6 points on a nightly basis throughout his career and should continue to have a large role in the 76ers' offense.

As for James, the 22-time All-Star recorded 20.9 points, 7.2 assists, 6.1 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 51.5 percent from the field during his 2025-26 season with the Los Angeles Lakers.

James knows what it takes to adapt to new teammates and win a championship, hoisting the Larry O'Brien Trophy with each of his three previous organizations including the Lakers, Cleveland Cavaliers and Miami Heat.

Philadelphia has made the playoffs in eight of the past nine years, but hasn't been able to advance beyond the second round since 2001.

As the new-look 76ers attempt to go on a deeper postseason run and contend for a title, James wants to ensure that everyone is on the same page.

articles.title: NBA Exec Picks Nikola Jokic over Wemby as No. 1 Player, Cites Spurs Star's Playoff 'Mistakes'
articles.summary: After Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokić was voted the NBA's best player over San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama as part of ESPN's NBA Rank 2026, an anonymous general manager explained the rationale behind their pick.
articles.body:
After Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokić was voted the NBA's best player over San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama as part of ESPN's NBA Rank 2026, an anonymous general manager explained the rationale behind their pick.

Speaking to ESPN's Ben Golliver about the distinction between Jokić and Wembanyama, the GM said, "Jokić makes his whole team better than anyone else. If you gave him and Wemby the same teammates, Denver would be better. Wemby being young doesn't bother me. What bothers me is that he made young mistakes in the playoffs."

Jokić finished atop ESPN's NBA Rank for a third consecutive year, while Wembanyama came in second one year after occupying the No. 5 spot.

Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who has won back-to-back NBA MVP awards, came in at No. 3.

Jokić, 31, is a three-time NBA MVP in his own right, and he has also finished second in the MVP voting three times, including last season.

On top of that, Jokić was named NBA Finals MVP when the Nuggets won their first-ever NBA championship in 2023.

Jokić's level of production is unmatched, as he averaged a triple-double for the second consecutive season in 2025-26, putting up 27.7 points, 12.9 rebounds and 10.7 assists per game.

Wemby, who is still just 22 years of age, finished third in the NBA MVP voting and was named NBA Defensive Player of the Year last season.

The 7'4" Frenchman averaged 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 3.1 blocks and 1.0 steal per game, and he played an integral role in the Spurs reaching the NBA Finals.

Wembanyama's numbers took a slight hit in the playoffs to the tune of 23.8 points, 10.9 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game, though, and he shot just 48.5 percent from the field compared to 51.2 percent during the regular season.

Even so, it is worth noting that last season was the first playoff run of Wembanyama's career, and one can only assume that he will improve in big games with experience.

For now, Jokić over Wembanyama is the popular opinion in the NBA, but after last season, the gap appears to be closing.

articles.title: Who is Sophie Cunningham? Fox Nation chronicles the WNBA star's rise from farm girl to women's sports advocate
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham's rise from Missouri farm girl to Indiana Fever star and women's sports advocate is explored in the "Who Is Sophie Cunningham?" special.
articles.body: Bold, beautiful and with a bullish resolve – Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has stormed onto the women's sports scene, commanding attention with her success on the court and unmistakable personality off it. "Men are attracted to her, and women want to be her," former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines said in Fox Nation's, "Who Is Sophie Cunningham?" Cunningham's appeal spans generations, with Gaines recalling the scores of young girls who lined up for a chance to meet the basketball star and get her autograph. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM ADDRESSES PERCEPTION THAT SHE IS THE 'SEX SYMBOL' OF THE WNBA From her humble beginnings as a Missouri farm girl to her rise in professional basketball and emergence as a voice in the "protect women's sports" movement, Cunningham's journey takes center stage in the new Fox Nation special. But the athlete fans see battling on the hardwood is only part of the story. "She's kind of like 100% tomboy and 100% feminine," Gaines said of Cunningham's nature. "Sophie is fun and kind and fierce and sassy and tough and cool because all those things make you cool." Gaines is joined in the special by others, including activist and former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom, who shed light on the personality, convictions and loyalty that have helped Cunningham build a following beyond basketball. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM ADDRESSES THE FALLOUT OVER HER STANCE ON TRANS ATHLETES NOT BELONGING IN WOMEN'S SPORTS In one instance, Kanter Freedom recalled hearing directly from Cunningham after he was ejected from an Aug. 23 WNBA game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever. "After the game, Sophie messaged me and said, 'So what happened?'" he said. Kanter Freedom said he explained the encounter to Cunningham but declined to reveal her response, teasing that the private exchange would "go viral" if made public. He had attended the game wearing a shirt defining a woman as an "adult human female." SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SENDS MESSAGE TO HER HATERS AFTER SAYING MEN DON'T BELONG IN WOMEN'S SPORTS "I was literally there just to support [Sophie]," he said. Cunningham herself has attracted attention for speaking publicly about the debate surrounding transgender participation in women's sports. She told ESPN earlier this year, "I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I'm like, 'I never once said that.' "I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think, with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room or young girls in sports who shouldn't have to go against biological men." Since her comments surfaced, the star athlete amassed support from the likes of politicians, former athletes and other girls fighting for the same cause. articles.title: Sparks Reportedly Fire Lynne Roberts After Missing WNBA Playoffs for 2nd Straight Season
articles.summary: After going 37-51 in two seasons under Lynne Roberts, the Los Angeles Sparks are making a change at head coach.
articles.body:
After going 37-51 in two seasons under Lynne Roberts, the Los Angeles Sparks are making a change at head coach.

Per ESPN's Ramona Shelburne , the Sparks fired Roberts on Friday after missing the playoffs in both years with her at the helm.

Following Thursday's 76-75 loss to the Golden State Valkyries to cap off the Sparks' 2026 season, Roberts was asked if she felt like she had done enough to earn a third year as head coach.

Playoff Bracket Predictions for Every Series 🔮

Caitlin Clark posts career low in blowout loss

"Yeah I think I have," she answered. "I think again, we've had two tough years of injuries, and I'm not trying to blame anything on that, it's just the reality. There has been a lot of change. Our president's been here … four months. So just again, so much change."

Roberts was hired in November 2024 by the previous front-office regime led by team president Christine Monjer and general manager Raegan Pebley.

Monjer stepped down in April and was replaced by Stacy Johns. Pebley and the Sparks announced a split on July 12 after the team got off to a 10-11 start this season.

Zach Knowlton and Nate Nielsen, who were assistants under Pebley, are currently serving as interim co-general managers for the Sparks.

Players who were expected to be key contributors have dealt with injuries. Cameron Brink has only played in 65 games through her first three seasons, though she did appear in a career-high 31 games in 2026.

Kelsey Plum was limited to 12 games due to an ankle sprain, then the Sparks traded her to the Phoenix Mercury in August.

The Sparks finished 16-28 this season under Roberts. They have missed the playoffs in six consecutive years, the longest active drought in the WNBA.

Los Angeles has now gone through four different head coaches since 2022. Derek Fisher left midway through the 2022 campaign, leading to Fred Williams finishing the year as interim head coach.

Curt Miller went 25-55 in two seasons before being replaced by Roberts going into the 2025 campaign.

articles.body: We had one play in the WNBA last night, and it went the exact opposite of how I expected it to go. articles.title: Storms Throw MLB Schedule Into Disarray Ahead of Playoffs: ‘Everything Is Up in the Air’
articles.summary: A powerful Nor’easter forecast for this weekend has forced scheduling changes for key games ahead of the MLB playoffs. The Chicago Cubs were supposed to play...
articles.body:
A powerful Nor'easter forecast for this weekend has forced scheduling changes for key games ahead of the MLB playoffs.

The Chicago Cubs were supposed to play the Boston Red Sox in their last games of the regular season on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, per a Friday, September 25 report by USA Today . But due to weather concerns, there will now be a doubleheaders on Friday, while Saturday's game could be moved to Florida's Tropicana Field because the Tampa Bay Rays will be finishing up the regular season in Philadelphia .

"Everything is up in the air," Cubs manager Craig Counsell told reporters on September 24, per the outlet. "Can we get out of Boston if we have to leave? There's a lot of uncertainty. We're prepared for the uncertainty. We know that plans are going to change this weekend."

Both the Cubs and the Red Sox have clinched wild-card spots in the playoffs.

Counsell has been concerned about how the changes could affect his team.

"They never move games up and especially within a five-day window of a starting rotation," he told reporters on September 23, per ESPN . "So we can't have somebody ready to pitch on Saturday. They just moved games up on us. I understand there's extenuating circumstances, but you just don't see that happening."

Boston manager Chad Tracy was optimistic.

"I'm planning on being ready to play those two games tomorrow," he told reporters on Thursday, per USA Today . "We should be able to get that in, even if the second game there might be like a little bit of drizzle."

Meanwhile, their longtime rivals are also scrambling. The New York Yankees , who also clinched a wild-card spot in the playoffs, will play in a doubleheader against the Baltimore Orioles on Friday, but their final regular season game on Sunday may get rained out as well, per The Athletic .

The Wild Card series kicks off on Tuesday, September 29.

articles.title: 5 Sparks coaching candidates after Lynne Roberts firing
articles.summary: The Sparks are making a coaching change amid their six-year playoff drought
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Sparks have seen enough from Lynne Roberts. After two straight sub .500 seasons under Roberts, the Sparks announced Friday they've fired the 51-year-old coach.

Los Angeles finished second to last in the WNBA in both turnovers and rebounding this season, preventing them from making a Western Conference push despite a productive campaign from Nneka Ogwumike .

"We are grateful to Lynne for the commitment and determination she brought to the role, which was evident all the way through our last game last night" Sparks special advisor Farhan Zaidi said in a statement . "Lynne has cared deeply about our organization and for our players and their development. We sincerely thank her for everything she has invested in the Sparks and wish her and her family the best moving forward."

Roberts came to the Sparks in November 2024 after a lengthy stint at Utah. She left the Utes four games into the 2024-25 season with an eye toward turning around a Sparks franchise that went four years without a playoff appearance, and instead the drought extended to six seasons.

Here are five coaching candidates who could possibly replace Roberts in Los Angeles.

After reaching the collegiate mountaintop with a national championship at UCLA, perhaps Close tries her hand at the WNBA. This one's unlikely, however, as UCLA holds a special place in Close's heart. That's where she began her coaching career in the 1990s, and John Wooden mentored her during those years.

Jenny Boucek, Indiana Pacers assistant coach

A longtime collaborator with Pacers coach Rick Carlisle, Boucek has spent the last five seasons in Indiana. She had a brief but rather unsuccessful stint as the Seattle Storm 's head coach from 2015-17. A Boucek hiring would continue the recent trend of NBA assistants getting WNBA head coaching jobs, with Chris DeMarco, Alex Sarama and Nate Tibbetts being the notable examples.

Brittni Donaldson, Portland Fire assistant coach/assistant GM

Donaldson is a rising star in both coaching and front office circles because of her unique ability to blend player development and analytics. She became an assistant coach of the Toronto Raptors at age 26 then had stints with the Detroit Pistons and Atlanta Hawks before taking on her dual role in Portland.

Eric Thibault, Minnesota Lynx associate head coach

The son of former WNBA coach Mike Thibault, Eric got fired as the Washington Mystics coach two seasons after taking over for his father in November 2022. He's since become a vital member of Cheryl Reeve's staff in Minnesota, where he very could win a title in a few weeks.

Kristi Toliver, Phoenix Mercury associate head coach

Toliver is a three-time WNBA All-Star who's spent the last three seasons as the Phoenix Mercury's associate head coach. She made history in 2018 by becoming the first active WNBA player to coach in the NBA, as she served as an assistant for the Washington Wizards.

articles.title: LeBron James Dishes on 'Intel' He Got About VJ Edgecombe After Making 76ers Decision
articles.summary: LeBron James says he learned while preparing to join the Philadelphia 76ers Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid weren't the only players taking on key leadership roles on last season's team.
articles.body:
LeBron James says he learned while preparing to join the Philadelphia 76ers Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid weren't the only players taking on key leadership roles on last season's team.

James said on Friday's Mind the Game podcast with Steve Nash he was told VJ Edgecombe also led the Sixers during his age-20 season.

"The intel that I've got from everyone is that this kid is beyond his years," James said about the 25:40 mark of the podcast. "They said he was actually one of the leaders of the team as a 20-year-old rookie.

"And not in a disrespectful manner. It's not like he was speaking just to be speaking, or thinking he's better than this guy. No. They say he speaks with an intelligence, confidence, natural, and works extremely hard, and he's a flat-out player."

James added he is expecting Edgecombe, who averaged 1.4 steals per game as a rookie, to join fellow newcomer Jaylen Brown in shaping the Sixers' defense next season.

"There's no reason he shouldn't be able to, if he really wants to, to be contending for an All-Defensive Team this year with his athleticism, with his length, with his speed," James said about Edgecombe.

James continued, "Obviously, I think JB's gonna set the tone, with his ability to guard, but I think VJ should be right there, just taking all the keys from JB, learning all the nuances, because he has all the tools."

Edgecombe, who impressed head coach Nick Nurse last season with his ability to quickly adjust to the NBA, will be taked with adapting to more changes this fall.

After taking on a significant ball-handling role for the Sixers as a rookie, Edgecombe could be destined for more off-ball play now that Brown and James are coming to Philadelphia.

The 76ers could get a first look at Edgecombe's role in the new starting lineup when training camp begins Sept. 29.

James is set to tip off his first season with the Sixers about three weeks later with an Oct. 20 matchup against the defending champion New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden.

articles.title: Luka Doncic Posts Behind-the-Scenes Video of Lakers 'Minicamp' in Slovenia Before NBA Season
articles.summary: This summer, Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Dončić hosted a minicamp for his teammates in his home country, Slovenia.
articles.body:
This summer, Los Angeles Lakers superstar Luka Dončić hosted a minicamp for his teammates in his home country, Slovenia.

On Friday, the six-time All-NBA First Team guard provided a behind-the-scenes look at the experience.

Dončić averaged an NBA-best 33.5 points per game in his first full season with the Lakers.

He's the clear top face of the Lakers now after LeBron James left in free agency for the Philadelphia 76ers. This squad has some promise thanks to the return of Austin Reaves and the additions of center Walker Kessler, wing Quentin Grimes and big man Sandro Mamukelashvili. First-round pick Cameron Carr also showed promise in NBA Summer League action and could be a strong asset off the bench.

The pieces are in place, and head coach JJ Redick likes how everything fits together on paper.

"I think we've always tried to give our players clearly defined roles. I think with this group, probably the first time in my three years here that I feel like the pieces actually fit together. So those roles probably get even more crystallized," Redick told reporters on Thursday.

"I'll give you the wing thing, like, there's a very clear ask for you to be able to play. And if you don't do those things, then you're not gonna play. That's just the reality. We've already had some of those conversations this week with our players.

"We have high, high confidence in these guys that they're going to buy into that. So, it's going to naturally create a lot of healthy competition. Everybody at some point, inevitably, will get a chance to impact our team and impact winning."

Of course, with this team having plenty of new faces, it's important for the squad to gel together on and off the court. Dončić, as the leader of this team, saw the importance of that and took lead on an important minicamp.

We'll see how this Lakers fit together soon enough when they open the season on Oct. 21 at home vs. the Golden State Warriors.

articles.title: LeBron James Says 76ers Will Need 'Bunker Mentality' to Combat Narratives During 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: LeBron James explained that the Philadelphia 76ers must prevent media narratives from affecting the team throughout the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
LeBron James explained that the Philadelphia 76ers must prevent media narratives from affecting the team throughout the 2026-27 season.

"We've got to have a bunker mentality," James said on his Mind the Game podcast (47:50 mark). "It's unfortunate, but very fortunate. The noise that comes with me, good, bad, indifferent. Everything, it's a little different. Is it warranted? I don't even know. If we have a bunker mentality on like, 'Nothing matters outside what we have.' Whether we're at the practice facility or we at the arena, nothing matters. Everyone's gonna have their opinion."

"The only thing that matters is what we preach every day and how we're gonna hold each other accountable," he added.

The 76ers wrapped up a busy offseason in which they added James and five-time All-Star Jaylen Brown to a core that includes Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

Philadelphia's moves have generated plenty of attention , which should only continue to grow once the 2026-27 season begins.

Embiid's injury history has been widely discussed in recent years, while Brown's relationship with former teammate Jayson Tatum was under the spotlight as he exited the Boston Celtics.

Maxey and Edgecombe proved to be an explosive young backcourt and helped Philadelphia make a second-round playoff appearance last season, but questions could arise if the guards aren't as productive with two new stars entering the mix.

As James gears up for his 24th year in the NBA, he doesn't want his new teammates to be impacted by any outside noise.

articles.title: LeBron, Joel Embiid Reportedly Had 'Multiple Lengthy Conversations' Before 76ers Contract
articles.summary: LeBron James reportedly had several "lengthy" talks with Joel Embiid before deciding to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason, according to ESPN's Dave McMenamin.
articles.body:
LeBron James reportedly had several "lengthy" talks with Joel Embiid before deciding to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason, according to ESPN's Dave McMenamin.

"I was told that there was multiple lengthy conversations in the leadup to LeBron deciding to pick the Philadelphia 76ers," McMenamin said Friday on NBA Today (2:20 mark of the video below). "They've talked about all sorts of things. Lineup combinations. What they like, what they don't like."

McMenamin's comments came the same day James publicly discussed his free agency decision for the first time on Friday's episode of Mind the Game with Steve Nash.

When asked what led him to decide to sign with the Sixers, James cited his friendship with Tyrese Maxey and the Sixers' signing of Jaylen Brown before describing Embiid as "one of the most important" factors.

"He's done everything in our league, and only thing he has not done, that's win a championship," James said about Embiid. "And I want to try and help him get that first one."

Embiid isn't the only Sixers star James spoke with before making his free agency decision. Maxey confirmed last month he and James had exchanged "a couple" phone calls and texts before the NBA's all-time leading scorer signed in Philadelphia.

James will now prepare to start his first training camp with the Sixers Tuesday before potentially making his regular-season debut for Philadelphia in an Oct. 20 season opener against the reigning champion New York Knicks.
